President Trump has pledged to retaliate against the European Union over what he claims are unfair fines targeting Apple and other American tech giants. Here are the details.

‘America is not a “PIGGYBANK” for Europe’

As spotted by CNBC, President Trump has published a lengthy post on Truth Social, threatening to impose a “substantial” tariff on the European Union in response to fines levied against Apple and other US tech giants.

In his post, Trump mentions the EU’s recent €890 million fine against Google for allegedly favoring its own services in violation of the Digital Markets Act. He also lists previous fines against Apple, Meta, and Amazon, accusing the EU of punishing American companies “for no reason at all”.

He goes on to threaten that the EU “will pay a very big price” for what he claims is an “illegal and highly unethical conduct,” and goes on to pledge that these “penalties will be entirely reversed.”

Here’s his post in full:

This is not the first time Trump has threatened tariffs in response to foreign penalties against Apple and other US tech companies. His administration previously described the EU’s 2025 fines against Apple and Meta as “economic extortion,” while warning that countries penalizing American businesses could face trade retaliation.

Specifically when it comes to Apple, Trump’s reference to a $15 billion fine appears to concern the EU’s long-running tax case against the company. In 2024, Europe’s highest court ordered Ireland to recover €13 billion in unpaid taxes from Apple, rather than imposing a fine payable to the EU. Apple was separately fined €570 million under the Digital Markets Act in April 2025.
